Unlock on #11725's close; re-verify the tripwire file exists on the merged ref.

The refusal-point question (refuse before the un-trash / refuse-and-compensate after / durability-channel report) is design *within* the ruled lock — if it grows product semantics beyond "packaged sets cannot be re-authored via restore" (e.g. behaviour changes for non-packaged rows), stop and fork to a decision card. Not foldable into #11725's probe PR — triage there was explicit.

> Blocked rather than queued because the tripwire this card must invert (`packaged-permission-set-restore-leg.test.ts`, MEASURED RESIDUAL case) lands in #11725's PR — there is nothing to invert until it merges. **Unlock on #11725's close; re-verify the tripwire file exists on the merged ref.**

**Limb 1 — #11725 is closed.** State `closed` / `completed`, **2026-08-25 05:42Z**, via PR #12021 (MERGED) — *"probe the trash/restore door for package-declared permission sets — pin the unreachability, measure the residual"*.

**Limb 2 — the tripwire exists on the merged ref**, measured on `origin/main` at `86df0c99e` rather than assumed from the PR having merged:

```
packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/packaged-permission-set-restore-leg.test.ts:276

```

⭐ That is the exact case this card must invert, present by name. ⚠️ Checking limb 2 separately was not ceremony: a merged PR is not proof its artifact survived review in the form the unlock depends on, and this card's whole deliverable is defined relative to that case's existence.

## ⚠️ This is the third card in this lane found parked on a discharged blocker today

#12009 (blocker closed 08-25 09:45Z) and #11833 (last dependency landed 08-25 19:49Z) were the first two. This one's blocker closed **08-25 05:42Z** — parked ~2 days.

All three were found by hand, ⛔ not by any patrol. A discharged block and a live one are indistinguishable at the label, and nothing scans the difference. Recording it here as well as on the others because three instances in one lane in one afternoon is a pattern, not a coincidence — and the two cards whose blocks I checked and found **live** (#11286, #12010) show the check is discriminating, not a rubber stamp.

## ⚠️ Clause ② — this seat's call: **YES**. `needs:contract-review` added.

`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` read **live** this pass at `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs:3813`: **`claude-fable-5`**.

The content limb is met directly, not by analogy: this card **adds a refusal where none exists today**. `restore` currently re-authors a packaged set with no lock consulted; after this card it is refused. That is *changing contract accept/reject behaviour* — the clause-② limb in its plainest form.

⚠️ I am aware the shape invites the opposite reading — "it only extends an already-ruled lock (#11513) to one more leg, so the decision is already made". The **decision** is indeed made; the clause-② gate is not about whether a decision exists, it is about what the change does to the accept/reject surface. And on a security-adjacent refusal the embarrassing direction is under-applying the control.

⇒ **This seat is below tier**: it may dispatch at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, but ⛔ will not clear the label, ⛔ will not flip a PR ready, and ⛔ will not arm auto-merge on this card.

## What the dispatch inherits unchanged from triage

- **Shape**: extend the #11702 lock to the `restore` leg **and invert the tripwire case in the same PR**. ⛔ Not foldable into #11725's probe PR — that was explicit, and #11725 is merged anyway.
- ⚠️ **The refusal-point question is design *within* the ruled lock**: refuse before the un-trash, refuse-and-compensate after, or report on a durability channel. ⭐ PR #11702's author gave the reason the save-door refusal cannot simply be copied here — *a throw after the record is already restored strands the caller with a healthy-looking row and no way to hear about it*, which is why the neighbouring paths catch rather than throw. So "add the same refusal" is **not** obviously the answer, and picking one is the real work.
- ⛔ **Fork condition, unchanged**: if it grows product semantics beyond *"packaged sets cannot be re-authored via restore"* — e.g. any behaviour change for **non-packaged** rows — stop and fork to a decision card.
- **Priority context, so nobody re-derives it**: currently unreachable (`restore` is outside the dispatch vocabulary; `API_METHOD_DERIVATION.restore.flag` is permanently false) ⇒ not P0. The reason to close it now is **#3146**, which makes it reachable. ⚠️ Both fronting gates have documented blind spots on exactly the packaged-set shape, so *"something else covers it"* is not an answer.
